summary: You made a strong, scenario-specific recommendation in Question 2 and showed a sound series-availability method in Question 3(a). To strengthen the rest of the submission, correct the availability arithmetic, explain the circuit-breaker states and CAP trade-off accurately, and make your quality-attribute measures and ADR consequences more complete.
next_steps: Revise Question 3(b) and (c): show the monthly downtime calculation clearly, and calculate end-to-end availability using all components rather than only the payment-provider pair.

In Questions 4 and 5, correct the circuit-breaker state transitions and explain that during a network partition a system must trade off consistency against availability; give a concrete technique for each case.

In Questions 1 and 6, make the availability response measure measurable and add a negative consequence to the ADR. Also bring Question 2 within 150 words and ensure every IEEE citation has a matching reference.

criteria.C1: In Question 1, you chose relevant attributes and linked them to the lunch peak and response time. To reach Excellent, correct the load figure (900 orders/hour is 15/minute, not about 150), complete both six-part scenarios, and replace “stay up most of the time” with a measurable order-placement availability target.
criteria.C2: Your modular-monolith recommendation in Question 2 is well matched to the five-person team and single-VM issue, and you acknowledge shared-process risk and limited independent scaling. You reached Excellent for this criterion; keep these scenario-specific trade-offs while tightening the answer to meet the word limit.
criteria.C3: In Question 3(a), you used the series method correctly. To reach Proficient, correct the arithmetic in (b) to about 5.0 hours of monthly downtime and in (c) include all components: approximately 99.80% end-to-end availability and 1.5 hours of monthly downtime. Show the working to the requested precision.
criteria.C4: You identified a relevant circuit breaker and explained fail-fast containment in Question 4. To reach Proficient, correct the sequence: Closed normally allows calls; failures open the breaker; after a wait, Half-open permits probes, with successful probes closing it and failures reopening it. For Excellent, also explain a drawback or tuning consideration.
criteria.C5: Your availability choice for menus and use of a cache with a TTL are appropriate. To reach Excellent in Question 5, explain that during a partition CAP requires a consistency-versus-availability trade-off, and name a concrete consistency technique for payments, such as an authoritative transactional ledger with idempotency keys.
criteria.C6: Your Question 6 ADR includes scenario-specific Context, Decision and positive consequences, including faster order responses. To reach Excellent, add a negative consequence, such as duplicate notifications from retrying queue delivery, and explain how idempotent consumption can address it.
criteria.C7: Your headings and writing are clear. To reach Excellent, keep every answer within 150 words, use precise terminology, and ensure all sources are cited in IEEE style. Question 2 exceeds the limit, and citation [2] in Question 4 needs a corresponding entry in the References section.
